symptoms: High fever, headache, body ache, fatigue
diagnosis: Viral fever — acute febrile illness, likely viral aetiology
advice: Rest adequately. Drink plenty of fluids. Avoid cold drinks. Tepid sponging for high fever. Report if temperature exceeds 104F.

symptoms: Fever, chills, generalised weakness, loss of appetite
diagnosis: Viral fever in a diabetic patient — close glycaemic monitoring required

prescription.condition: Take after each loose stool or if unable to eat meals

advice: Monitor blood sugar every 6 hours. Maintain soft light diet. Avoid NSAIDs. Continue Metformin with food. Seek care if sugar exceeds 300.

symptoms: Fever with chills, joint pain, mild breathlessness
diagnosis: Viral fever with arthralgia in elderly hypertensive patient
advice: Avoid NSAIDs due to hypertension and age. Monitor BP daily. Bed rest. Light diet with adequate fluids.

symptoms: Fever, runny nose, sneezing, mild throat pain, watery eyes
diagnosis: Viral fever with upper respiratory tract infection (URTI)
advice: Steam inhalation twice daily. Warm fluids. Avoid cold exposure. Rest.

symptoms: High fever, severe body ache, retro-orbital pain, rash on trunk
diagnosis: Probable dengue fever — close monitoring advised
advice: Strictly avoid NSAIDs and aspirin. Monitor platelet count every 48 hours. Drink 3–4 litres of fluid daily. Report immediately if platelet drops below 1 lakh or bleeding occurs.

symptoms: Fever with severe throat pain, difficulty swallowing, body ache
advice: Warm salt water gargles. Soft diet. Complete antibiotic course. Avoid cold drinks.

symptoms: Fever, joint pains, extreme fatigue, mild rash on arms
diagnosis: Viral fever with arthralgia — possible chikungunya or viral exanthem
advice: Continue Levothyroxine. Rest joint with mild warm compress. Adequate hydration. Follow up in 5 days.

symptoms: Fever, headache, nausea, loss of appetite, yellow tinge in eyes
diagnosis: Viral hepatitis — likely Hepatitis A, jaundice present

prescription.condition: Take only if nausea is significant or vomiting occurs

advice: Strict bed rest. High-carbohydrate low-fat diet. Avoid fatty foods, alcohol, and hepatotoxic drugs. Follow up in 1 week with LFT.

symptoms: Runny nose, sneezing, nasal congestion, mild headache, no fever
additionalNotes: Seasonal allergic rhinitis, known dust allergy
diagnosis: Allergic rhinitis — triggered by seasonal allergens

prescription.condition: Use only if congestion is severe; do not exceed 3 days

advice: Avoid dust exposure. Use N95 mask in dusty environments. Steam inhalation for congestion. Saline nasal rinse morning and night.

symptoms: Sneezing, runny nose, mild sore throat, no fever

prescription.condition: Take only if headache or discomfort

advice: Warm fluids. Avoid decongestants with pseudoephedrine (raises BP). Steam inhalation. Hand hygiene.

symptoms: Runny nose, sneezing, watery eyes, nasal congestion, mild cough
diagnosis: Common cold with mild allergic component
advice: Keep pets out of bedroom. Use air purifier if possible. Warm salt water gargles. Plenty of fluids.

symptoms: Nasal discharge, sneezing, nasal congestion, no fever
diagnosis: Common cold in diabetic hypertensive patient
advice: Avoid pseudoephedrine-containing cold medicines. Monitor BP and blood sugar. Warm fluids. Continue regular medications.

symptoms: Nasal congestion, loss of smell and taste, mild headache
advice: Smell training with strong scents (lemon, clove) twice daily. Nasal saline rinse. Avoid chemical irritants.

symptoms: Dry cough, tickling in throat, worsens at night
diagnosis: Post-viral dry cough — irritant cough reflex
advice: Steam inhalation. Avoid cold drinks and AC. Sleep with head slightly elevated. Avoid throat clearing.

symptoms: Productive cough with yellowish sputum, mild fever, wheezing
additionalNotes: Peak flow reduced, no chest pain
diagnosis: Acute exacerbation of asthma with productive cough — likely infective trigger

prescription.condition: Use if wheezing or breathlessness occurs; can repeat every 4–6 hours

advice: Continue Budesonide inhaler. Avoid cold air, dust, and smoke. Use spacer with inhaler. Follow up if breathlessness worsens.

symptoms: Productive cough with greenish sputum, fever, chest discomfort
diagnosis: Acute bronchitis — bacterial superinfection likely in smoker

prescription.condition: Take only if fever present

advice: Stop smoking immediately. Steam inhalation. Complete antibiotic course. Follow up if chest pain or breathlessness develops.

symptoms: Dry cough, irritation in throat, runny nose, post-nasal drip
additionalNotes: Cough worse in morning and night, no fever
diagnosis: Cough due to post-nasal drip — upper airway cough syndrome
advice: Sleep with head elevated. Nasal saline rinse twice daily. Avoid dairy products at night. Follow up in 2 weeks.

symptoms: Sore throat, difficulty swallowing, fever, swollen neck glands
advice: Complete antibiotic course. Warm salt water gargles 4 times a day. Soft diet. Cold ice cream can soothe throat.

symptoms: Sore throat, hoarseness of voice, difficulty swallowing

prescription.condition: Dissolve slowly in mouth for throat pain relief

advice: Voice rest — avoid speaking loudly. Warm honey-lemon tea. Avoid cold drinks.

symptoms: Sore throat, fever 101F, swollen tonsils, bad breath
advice: ENT referral advised for tonsillectomy evaluation. Complete antibiotics. Warm gargles. Soft diet.

symptoms: Throat pain with low-grade fever, no exudate, mild cough
advice: Warm salt water gargles. Avoid cold and sour food. Honey in warm water. Follow up only if fever worsens.

symptoms: Throbbing headache, nausea, sensitivity to light and sound

prescription.condition: Take at onset of migraine; may repeat after 2 hours if no relief; max 2 doses/day
Take if nausea accompanies headache

advice: Identify and avoid triggers (stress, bright light, irregular sleep). Dark quiet room during attack. Stay hydrated.

symptoms: Headache at back of head, nausea, neck stiffness

prescription.condition: Take only if headache is present

advice: Monitor BP twice daily. Reduce salt intake. Avoid stress. Return immediately if BP exceeds 180/110.

symptoms: Tension headache, bilateral pressure, worse with stress and screen time
additionalNotes: IT professional, 10 hours screen time daily

prescription.condition: Take only if paracetamol gives inadequate relief

advice: 20-20-20 rule for screen use. Neck stretches. Regular sleep schedule. Reduce caffeine. Yoga or meditation for stress.

symptoms: Recurrent headaches, pressure around eyes, facial pain, nasal congestion
additionalNotes: Worse in mornings, previous sinusitis history

prescription.condition: Take only when headache is troublesome

advice: Steam inhalation twice daily. Nasal saline irrigation. Sleep with head elevated. ENT referral if no improvement in 2 weeks.

symptoms: Burning in chest, sour belching, upper abdominal pain, worse after spicy food

prescription.condition: Take if burning occurs between meals or at bedtime

advice: Eat small frequent meals. No spicy, oily, or acidic food. Avoid lying down for 2 hours after meals. Elevate head of bed.

symptoms: Acidity, bloating, heartburn, upper abdominal discomfort after meals
diagnosis: GERD / Functional dyspepsia in diabetic patient
advice: Small frequent meals. Avoid lying after meals. Reduce tea and coffee. Continue diabetes medications. Monitor blood sugar.

symptoms: Upper abdominal pain, burning epigastric pain, worse on empty stomach
additionalNotes: Relief after eating, NSAID use history
diagnosis: Peptic ulcer disease — NSAID-induced gastritis likely

prescription.condition: Take if pain occurs between meals

advice: Avoid NSAIDs, aspirin, and alcohol. Eat regularly. No spicy food. Follow up with endoscopy if no improvement in 4 weeks.

symptoms: Heartburn, regurgitation, belching, throat irritation
advice: Weight reduction target BMI <25. Elevate head of bed by 6 inches. Eat dinner 3 hours before sleep. Avoid tea and coffee after 6pm.

symptoms: Stomach cramps, loose watery stools, nausea, vomiting, mild fever

prescription.condition: Sip 200ml after each loose stool
Take only if vomiting is present

advice: Bland diet — rice, curd, banana. Avoid oily food. No milk. Strict hand hygiene. Seek emergency if unable to retain fluids.

symptoms: Cramping abdominal pain around umbilicus, watery diarrhoea, no fever
diagnosis: Acute gastroenteritis — possibly irritable bowel exacerbation

prescription.condition: Take only if abdominal cramps are severe

advice: Light diet. Avoid raw vegetables and dairy. Manage stress. Probiotics (curd) can help after recovery.

symptoms: Loose stools, abdominal pain, nausea, dehydration
additionalNotes: Metformin can cause diarrhoea, blood sugar dropping
diagnosis: Acute gastroenteritis with dehydration in diabetic patient

prescription.condition: Take only if nausea or vomiting is troublesome

advice: Temporarily reduce Metformin dose until stools normalise. Monitor blood sugar every 4 hours. Light diet — rice and curd. Seek care if unable to retain fluids.

symptoms: Severe watery diarrhoea, vomiting, abdominal cramps, weakness
diagnosis: Acute infectious gastroenteritis — likely traveller's diarrhoea

prescription.condition: Take if vomiting prevents ORS intake

advice: Drink only bottled or boiled water. Strict hand hygiene. Avoid raw food while travelling. Seek IV fluids if unable to retain oral intake.

symptoms: Watery diarrhoea 6–8 times per day, rice-water stools, muscle cramps
diagnosis: Suspected cholera — acute profuse watery diarrhoea

prescription.condition: Sip continuously; target 500ml/hour

advice: Urgent referral to hospital for IV fluids. Strict isolation. Report to public health authority. Boil all water.

symptoms: Loose stools alternating with constipation, lower abdominal pain, bloating

prescription.condition: Take only when abdominal cramps are present

advice: High-fibre diet. Identify and avoid trigger foods. Stress management — yoga or meditation. Probiotics helpful.

symptoms: Nausea, vomiting 3–4 times, upper abdominal pain, no diarrhoea
additionalNotes: Ate heavy oily meal last night
diagnosis: Acute gastritis with vomiting — dietary indiscretion

prescription.condition: Take if nausea or vomiting occurs

advice: Nothing by mouth for 2 hours after vomiting. Then sip ORS. Light diet. Avoid oily food for 1 week.

symptoms: Vomiting, nausea, dizziness, headache
advice: Avoid reading during travel. Look at horizon. Sit in front seat. Ginger candy can help. Avoid heavy meals before travel.

symptoms: Nausea in the morning, vomiting 2–3 times, food aversion, fatigue
diagnosis: Nausea and vomiting of early pregnancy (morning sickness)
advice: Small frequent meals. Avoid strong smells. Ginger tea may help. Stay hydrated. OB referral for antenatal care.

symptoms: No bowel movement for 5 days, hard stool, straining, bloating

prescription.condition: Take only if no bowel movement for 3 days

advice: Increase fruits, vegetables, and water intake. Walk 30 minutes daily. Do not suppress urge to defecate.

symptoms: Chronic constipation, bloating, low appetite
advice: Repeat TSH. Increase fibre intake. Warm water on waking. Light exercise. Review Levothyroxine dose with endocrinologist.

symptoms: Constipation, hard stools, anal pain while defecating, occasional blood in stool

prescription.condition: Use only if no bowel movement for 4+ days
Apply to anal area at bedtime for pain and swelling

advice: High fibre diet. Increase water intake to 3 litres/day. Sitz bath twice daily. Avoid straining. Surgical referral if not improving.

symptoms: Lower back pain, radiating to left leg, worsens on sitting or bending
diagnosis: Lumbar disc herniation with left-sided sciatica

prescription.condition: Take for nerve pain/tingling; may cause drowsiness

advice: Hot or cold pack on lower back. Physiotherapy referral. Ergonomic chair. Avoid lifting heavy weights. MRI lumbar spine if no improvement.

symptoms: Severe lower back pain, difficulty standing, worse in morning
additionalNotes: DEXA scan showed osteoporosis, sudden onset

prescription.condition: Apply topically to lower back; do not use if skin is broken
Take with full glass of water; remain upright for 30 minutes

advice: Urgent X-ray lumbar spine. Fall prevention at home. Physiotherapy. Continue calcium and Vit D. Avoid oral NSAIDs in elderly.

symptoms: Lower back pain, muscle spasm, stiffness, worsens with movement
advice: Hot pack to lumbar area. Short rest followed by gentle walking. No heavy lifting for 2 weeks. Physiotherapy if pain persists.

symptoms: Lower back pain radiating to buttocks, no leg weakness
additionalNotes: No red flag signs, no bladder issues
diagnosis: Mechanical lower back pain — sacroiliac joint dysfunction
advice: Physiotherapy referral. Hot pack. Core strengthening exercises. Avoid prolonged standing. Avoid NSAIDs due to hypertension.

symptoms: Lower back pain, chronic, worse in morning, associated with stiffness lasting >1 hour
diagnosis: Chronic lower back pain with likely spondylitis; elevated uric acid contributing to inflammation
advice: Avoid NSAIDs (renal risk in diabetes). Physiotherapy. Low-purine diet. Increase water intake. Rheumatology referral for HLA-B27 testing.

symptoms: Knee pain, bilateral, worse on climbing stairs and sitting to standing

prescription.condition: Apply to knee joints for local pain relief

advice: Weight reduction. Low-impact exercise (swimming, cycling). Avoid squatting and sitting on floor. Physiotherapy.

symptoms: Knee and finger joint pain, morning stiffness >1 hour, swelling
advice: Warm water hand soaks morning. Joint protection. Continue Methotrexate and Folic acid. Rheumatology follow-up.

symptoms: Severe pain and swelling in right big toe, redness, warm to touch, unable to walk
additionalNotes: Uric acid 9.2, had beer last night
diagnosis: Acute gout attack — first metatarsophalangeal joint
advice: Ice pack on toe. Elevate foot. Strict avoidance of alcohol, red meat, and organ meats. Increase water. Continue Allopurinol.

symptoms: Generalised body ache, muscle pain, stiffness all over, fatigue
additionalNotes: No fever, mild stress at work
advice: Gentle yoga and stretching. Improve sleep hygiene. Stress management. Check Vit D and B12 levels.

symptoms: Muscle pain in legs and arms after intense workout, stiffness
additionalNotes: Gym, first time back after 3 months

prescription.condition: Apply to sore muscles
Take only if pain is significant

advice: Light stretching. Warm bath. Gradually increase workout intensity. Adequate protein intake. 48-hour rest between sessions.

symptoms: Itchy skin rash on arms and trunk, hives, swelling, redness
additionalNotes: Started new soap, no food change
diagnosis: Contact dermatitis — allergic reaction to topical product

prescription.condition: Apply to affected skin area once daily
Apply for itching relief

advice: Discontinue new soap. Use fragrance-free soap. Avoid scratching. Patch test new products. Cotton clothing.

symptoms: Urticaria (hives), severe itching all over body, mild lip swelling
additionalNotes: Ate prawns at a party, first episode

prescription.condition: Use only if throat swelling, breathing difficulty, or collapse occurs — then call emergency

advice: Strictly avoid shellfish and seafood. Carry antihistamine at all times. Allergy testing. ER immediately if throat swells.

symptoms: Dry, scaly, itchy skin patches on elbows and behind knees, oozing

prescription.condition: Apply only to affected patches; do not use on face

advice: Moisturise immediately after bathing. Lukewarm baths only. Cotton clothing. Identify and avoid triggers. Dermatology referral.

symptoms: Scaly plaques on scalp and elbows, silver scales, itching
diagnosis: Plaque psoriasis — scalp and extensor surfaces

prescription.condition: Apply to plaques on elbows; avoid face and folds
Take only if itching is significant

advice: Avoid triggers: stress, alcohol, trauma. Sun exposure (10–15 min) can help. Dermatology referral for biologics if extensive.

symptoms: Burning urination, frequent urination, lower abdominal pain, urine colour dark
additionalNotes: Urine routine shows pus cells ++, no fever

prescription.condition: Take for burning relief; urine will turn orange — normal

advice: Drink 3 litres of water daily. Urinate after intercourse. Avoid holding urine. Cotton underwear. Follow up with urine culture.

symptoms: Burning urination, fever, flank pain, chills
diagnosis: Pyelonephritis — upper UTI in diabetic patient
advice: High fluid intake. Urine culture and sensitivity. Monitor blood sugar closely. Consider hospitalisation if vomiting prevents oral intake.

symptoms: Recurrent UTI — burning urination, frequency, lower abdominal pain
advice: Gynaecology referral for recurrent UTI workup. Voiding diary. Post-coital voiding. D-mannose powder may help. Urine culture follow-up.

symptoms: Burning urination, hesitancy, incomplete voiding, fever
diagnosis: UTI with BPH — complicated UTI in elderly male

prescription.condition: Take only if fever or discomfort

advice: Urology referral for BPH management. Increase fluid intake. Avoid alcohol and caffeine. Continue Tamsulosin.

symptoms: BP check — no symptoms, regular review
diagnosis: Hypertension — sub-optimally controlled, add-on therapy needed
advice: DASH diet. Reduce salt to <5g/day. 30 min walk daily. Quit smoking. Recheck BP in 2 weeks. Fasting lipid profile.

symptoms: Headache, dizziness, BP 158/96 at home readings
advice: Take Levothyroxine 30 min before breakfast on empty stomach. BP diary. Recheck TSH in 6 weeks. Reduce salt and stress.

symptoms: Dizziness on standing, weakness, BP 100/68 (low today)
diagnosis: Orthostatic hypotension — over-treated hypertension with hypoglycaemia
advice: Reduce Amlodipine back to 5mg. Rise slowly from sitting/lying. Monitor BP and blood sugar daily. Return if fainting occurs.

symptoms: High BP 168/100, palpitations, mild chest tightness
additionalNotes: Stressful week at work, no chest pain at rest
advice: Stress management. Reduce salt. Moderate exercise. ECG. Recheck BP in 1 week. Avoid caffeine.

symptoms: BP monitoring visit, BP 135/85, no symptoms
diagnosis: Hypertension — well controlled, continue current regimen
advice: Continue current medication. Monitor BP weekly. Low-sodium diet. 30 min walk. Next review in 3 months with lipid profile.

symptoms: Increased thirst, frequent urination, fatigue, blurred vision
advice: Diabetic diet. No refined carbohydrates. 30 min walk after meals. Self-monitoring of blood sugar. Ophthalmology referral for blurred vision.

symptoms: Foot numbness, tingling, burning pain in feet at night
advice: Inspect feet daily. Avoid walking barefoot. Proper-fitting shoes. Tight glycaemic control. Podiatry referral.

symptoms: Low blood sugar episode — sweating, trembling, palpitations, confusion

prescription.condition: Take immediately if blood sugar <70 or symptoms of hypoglycaemia occur; recheck after 15 min

advice: Never skip meals. Carry glucose tablets at all times. Eat regular small meals. Educate family on hypoglycaemia management. Recheck blood sugar in 15 min after treatment.

symptoms: Routine check — no symptoms, fasting sugar 110
diagnosis: Type 2 diabetes mellitus — well controlled, continue regimen
advice: Continue current regimen. HbA1c every 3 months. Annual eye, foot, and kidney check. Low-GI diet. Regular exercise.

symptoms: Dizziness, spinning sensation, nausea, worse with head movement

prescription.condition: Take if nausea accompanies vertigo episodes

advice: Epley manoeuvre to be performed by physiotherapist. Avoid sudden head movements. Sleep with head elevated. Avoid driving during acute episodes.

symptoms: Sudden onset severe dizziness, room spinning, vomiting, imbalance

prescription.condition: Take only if vomiting is significant

advice: Bed rest. ENT referral. Vestibular rehabilitation exercises after acute phase. Avoid driving. Follow up in 3 days.

symptoms: Giddiness on standing, unsteadiness, mild headache
additionalNotes: BP drops on standing, low-sodium diet recently started
advice: Rise slowly. Increase dietary salt slightly. Increase fluid intake. Review Amlodipine dose. Compression stockings may help.

symptoms: Difficulty falling asleep, waking up at night, unrefreshing sleep, daytime fatigue
additionalNotes: Work stress, using phone in bed

prescription.condition: Take only if unable to sleep despite melatonin; avoid long-term use

advice: No screens 1 hour before bed. Fixed sleep-wake time. Dark, cool bedroom. No caffeine after 3pm. Cognitive Behavioural Therapy for insomnia (CBT-I) referral.

symptoms: Snoring, gasping during sleep, excessive daytime sleepiness, morning headache
diagnosis: Obstructive sleep apnoea — suspected, needs sleep study
advice: Urgent sleep study (polysomnography). Weight loss. Side-sleeping. Avoid alcohol before bed. CPAP therapy likely needed. ENT referral.

symptoms: Insomnia, anxiety, heart pounding at night, excessive worry
additionalNotes: Recent job change, no prior psychiatric history

prescription.condition: Short-term use only; taper after 2 weeks

advice: Counselling or CBT referral. Breathing exercises. Journalling. Limit caffeine. Review in 2 weeks.

symptoms: Generalised weakness, fatigue, pale skin, shortness of breath on exertion, palpitations
advice: Iron-rich diet: spinach, jaggery, dates, lentils. Avoid tea/coffee with meals. Recheck Hb in 4 weeks. If <7 g/dL, IV iron or transfusion referral.

symptoms: Fatigue, weight gain, cold intolerance, dry skin, hair fall, constipation
advice: Take Levothyroxine on empty stomach, 30 min before breakfast. No soy/calcium within 4 hours. Recheck TSH in 6 weeks. Biotin supplement for hair.

symptoms: Extreme fatigue, weakness, pins and needles in hands and feet, forgetfulness
advice: Include eggs, dairy, or B12-fortified foods if vegetarian. Injectable B12 if very low. Recheck B12 in 8 weeks.

symptoms: Red, painful eye, discharge, crusting on eyelids on waking

prescription.condition: Use as lubricant for dryness or irritation

advice: Do not touch eyes. Wash hands frequently. Do not share towels. Use fresh tissue to clean discharge. No contact lenses for 2 weeks.

symptoms: Ear pain, pulling sensation in ear, discharge from ear, reduced hearing
additionalNotes: Swam in pool recently, outer ear tender on movement

prescription.condition: Take for ear pain

advice: Keep ear dry. Avoid swimming. No ear buds or cotton swabs. Warm compress on ear. ENT referral if not improving in 5 days.

symptoms: Ear pain, fever, decreased hearing, irritability
additionalNotes: Child, recent cold, tympanic membrane bulging

prescription.condition: Give if fever or pain

advice: Complete antibiotic course. Follow up with ENT in 1 week. No water in ears. Check hearing after infection resolves.

symptoms: Watery itchy eyes, foreign body sensation, no discharge
diagnosis: Dry eye syndrome with allergic conjunctivitis
advice: Reduce contact lens wear. 20-20-20 rule. Humidifier in office. Omega-3 supplements. Ophthalmology review.

symptoms: Sharp chest pain on one side, worse on deep breathing, no shortness of breath, no fever
additionalNotes: Pain reproducible on pressing chest wall, recent cough

prescription.condition: Apply locally to tender chest area

advice: ECG to rule out cardiac cause. Avoid heavy lifting. Heat pad on chest. Follow up if pain worsens or spreads to arm/jaw.

symptoms: Chest pain left-sided, radiating to left arm, sweating, breathlessness
diagnosis: Acute coronary syndrome — STEMI suspected, urgent referral

prescription.condition: Chew immediately
Give immediately

advice: EMERGENCY — Call ambulance immediately. Lie patient flat. Oxygen if available. Do NOT drive yourself. Transfer to nearest cardiac centre for primary PCI.

symptoms: Chest tightness, sharp pain left side, worse lying down, better sitting forward
additionalNotes: Recent viral illness, pericardial friction rub
advice: Restrict physical activity for 3 months. Echocardiogram. Cardiology referral. No sports until pain-free for 3 months.

symptoms: Neck pain, stiffness, pain radiating to right shoulder and arm, numbness in fingers
diagnosis: Cervical spondylosis with radiculopathy — C5-C6 level

prescription.condition: Take for nerve pain/numbness

advice: Cervical pillow. Physiotherapy and cervical traction. Ergonomic workstation. MRI cervical spine. Reduce screen time.

symptoms: Wrist pain and swelling, numbness in thumb, index and middle fingers, worse at night
additionalNotes: Positive Tinel's sign, frequent computer work
advice: Wrist splint at night. Ergonomic keyboard. Wrist stretches. Physiotherapy. Orthopaedic referral for steroid injection if no improvement.

symptoms: Neck pain and stiffness following road accident, unable to turn head
advice: Soft cervical collar for first 72 hours. Ice pack first 48 hours, then warm. Physiotherapy. Avoid driving for 1 week.

symptoms: High fever, chills, body ache, high BP 170/100, blood sugar 320, loss of appetite
additionalNotes: HbA1c 10.2, on max oral meds, urine ketones negative
diagnosis: Viral fever with uncontrolled diabetes and hypertension — complex case requiring close monitoring

prescription.condition: Monitor fasting sugar; adjust dose if <80 or >200
Take if unable to eat meals

advice: Monitor blood sugar every 4–6 hours. Monitor BP twice daily. High fluid intake. Soft diet. Consider hospitalisation if fever >104F or sugar >400. Avoid NSAIDs strictly.

symptoms: Productive cough, thick yellowish sputum, low-grade fever, chest heaviness
additionalNotes: Non-smoker, office worker, recent cold 2 weeks ago
diagnosis: Acute bronchitis with secondary bacterial infection

prescription.condition: Take only if fever is present

advice: Steam inhalation twice daily. Drink warm fluids. Complete antibiotic course. Follow up if breathlessness develops.

symptoms: Knee swelling, warmth, pain, inability to fully extend knee
diagnosis: Reactive arthritis — knee effusion, likely post-viral

prescription.condition: Apply locally to swollen knee

advice: RICE — Rest, Ice, Compression, Elevation. Orthopaedic referral for aspiration if swelling worsens. Avoid oral NSAIDs due to age.

symptoms: Facial acne, painful pimples on cheeks and forehead, oily skin

prescription.condition: Apply to acne spots at night only; use sunscreen in morning

advice: Non-comedogenic moisturiser and sunscreen. Avoid picking pimples. Oil-free makeup. Gynaecology referral for hormonal workup. Reduce dairy.

symptoms: Chronic cough for 2 months, white frothy sputum, no fever, mild breathlessness on exertion
additionalNotes: Smoker 20 years, FEV1/FVC ratio reduced on spirometry
diagnosis: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) — mild, tobacco-related

prescription.condition: Use when short of breath; not more than 4 times/day

advice: QUIT SMOKING — most important intervention. Pulmonology referral for full PFT. Flu and pneumococcal vaccines. Breathing exercises.

symptoms: Heavy painful periods, pelvic pain, bloating, pain during intercourse
additionalNotes: Periods last 8 days, clots, no pregnancy

prescription.condition: Take during menstrual days only, starting 1 day before expected period
Take during heavy flow days only

advice: Gynaecology referral for pelvic ultrasound and laparoscopy. Hormonal therapy may be considered. Iron-rich diet. Track menstrual cycle.

symptoms: Severe menstrual cramps, nausea, headache, unable to attend college during periods
additionalNotes: Primary dysmenorrhoea, no structural cause found

prescription.condition: Take starting 1 day before period and continue for first 2–3 days
Take if mefenamic acid alone is insufficient for pain

advice: Heat pad on lower abdomen. Omega-3 supplements. Regular exercise throughout the month reduces cramps. Gynaecology referral if very severe.

symptoms: Burning and tingling in right foot, numbness between 3rd and 4th toes, worsens walking
diagnosis: Morton's neuroma — compression neuropathy of interdigital nerve

prescription.condition: Take for burning/tingling nerve pain

advice: Wide-toed shoes. Metatarsal pads. Orthopaedic insoles. Weight reduction. Orthopaedic referral for steroid injection if no relief.

symptoms: Hot flushes, night sweats, mood swings, irregular periods, vaginal dryness
additionalNotes: Age 48, FSH elevated, LMP 3 months ago

prescription.condition: Take for hot flushes; may cause mild drowsiness

advice: Gynaecology referral for HRT discussion. Cool bedroom. Breathable clothing. Avoid caffeine and alcohol. Soy-rich diet. DEXA scan for bone density.

symptoms: Severe unilateral headache around left eye, tearing, redness, nasal congestion, attacks last 45 minutes and occur daily at same time

prescription.condition: Use at attack onset; max 1 dose per 24 hours

advice: 100% oxygen at 7–12 L/min for 15 min aborts most attacks — arrange home oxygen. Avoid alcohol and smoking during cluster period. Neurology referral.

symptoms: Pain and swelling in right heel, worse in morning first steps, improves after walking
additionalNotes: Overweight, stands for long hours at work

prescription.condition: Apply to heel area morning and night

advice: Heel cup or silicone insole. Calf stretches before getting out of bed. Avoid walking barefoot. Weight reduction. Physiotherapy. Orthopaedic referral if no improvement in 6 weeks.

symptoms: Itching and burning in scalp, white flakes on scalp and shoulders, mild redness

prescription.condition: Apply only if itching is severe

advice: Use antidandruff shampoo alternating with regular shampoo. Avoid harsh hair products. Dermatology referral if no response in 4 weeks.

symptoms: Painful blisters on lips, tingling before blisters appear, recurrent
additionalNotes: Second episode this year, stressed recently

prescription.condition: Apply at first sign of tingling for best effect
Take for severe or spreading lesions

advice: Avoid kissing or sharing utensils during active lesions. Sunscreen on lips prevents UV-triggered recurrence. Lysine supplement may reduce frequency.
